thescelosaurus:enwiki:4.title: Thescelosaurus (T. edmontonensis, revision, and T. garbanii)

facts.statement: Bugenasaura is a synonym of the genus Thescelosaurus.
facts.quote: synonyms: Bugenasaura Galton, 1995

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus edmontonensis was named by Sternberg in 1940 but is considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: subdivision: T. edmontonensis Sternberg, 1940 (nomen dubium)

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus is the namesake genus of the family Thescelosauridae.
facts.quote: Thescelosaurus is the eponymous member of its family, the Thescelosauridae.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurids are classified either as basal ornithopods or as a group outside ornithopods within Neornithischia.
facts.quote: Thescelosaurids are either considered to be basal ("primitive") ornithopods, or are placed outside of this group within the broader group Neornithischia.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus was named and described in 1913 by the paleontologist Charles W. Gilmore.
facts.quote: It was named and described in 1913 by the paleontologist Charles W. Gilmore

facts.statement: The species T. garbanii was named in 1976 and T. assiniboiensis was named in 2011.
facts.quote: Two other species, T. garbanii and T. assiniboiensis, were named in 1976 and 2011, respectively.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the late Maastrichtian age.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous (late Maastrichtian),

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus lived until around 66 million years ago, shortly before the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event.
facts.quote: Living during the late Maastrichtian age, it was among the last of the non-avian dinosaurs before the entire group went extinct during the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event around 66 million years ago.

facts.statement: Fossils of Thescelosaurus have been found across a wide range in western North America.
facts.quote: Thescelosaurus has been found across a wide geographic range across western North America.

facts.statement: A near-complete skeleton of Thescelosaurus was discovered in July 1891 by John Bell Hatcher and William H. Utterback along Doegie Creek in Niobrara County, Wyoming.
facts.quote: In July 1891, the fossil hunter John Bell Hatcher, who had been hired by Marsh, and his assistant William H. Utterback discovered a near-complete skeleton of a small herbivorous dinosaur along Doegie Creek in Niobrara County, Wyoming, in rocks of the Lance Formation.

facts.statement: Charles W. Gilmore published the preliminary description of Thescelosaurus neglectus in 1913.
facts.quote: In 1913, Gilmore published a preliminary description naming the new genus and species Thescelosaurus neglectus.

facts.statement: Adult Thescelosaurus measured approximately 3 to 4 meters in length and weighed between 200 and 300 kilograms.
facts.quote: Adult Thescelosaurus would have measured roughly 3-4 m long and probably weighed 200 to 300 kg.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus was a bipedal dinosaur with a long tail that made up half its body length and was stiffened by ossified tendons.
facts.quote: It moved on two legs, and its body was counter-balanced by its long tail, which made up half of the body length and was stiffened by rod-like ossified tendons.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had a long, low snout ending in a toothless beak.
facts.quote: The animal had a long, low snout that ended in a toothless beak.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus possessed more teeth than related genera, and these teeth varied in type.
facts.quote: It had more teeth than related genera, and the teeth were of different types.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had five fingers on its hands and four toes on its feet.
facts.quote: The hand bore five fingers, and the foot four toes.

facts.statement: Thin plates were found next to the ribs of Thescelosaurus, though their function remains unclear.
facts.quote: Thin plates are found next to the ribs' sides, the function of which is unclear.

facts.statement: Scale impressions have been found on the leg of one Thescelosaurus specimen.
facts.quote: Scale impressions are known from the leg of one specimen.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus was an herbivore that likely fed selectively, based on its teeth and narrow snout.
facts.quote: An herbivore, Thescelosaurus was likely a selective feeder, as indicated by its teeth and narrow snout.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had robust limbs with a femur longer than its tibia, suggesting it was not adapted for running.
facts.quote: Its limbs were robust, and its femur (thigh bone) was longer than its tibia (shin bone), suggesting that it was not adapted to running.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had a comparatively small brain, which may indicate it lived in small groups of two to three individuals.
facts.quote: Its brain was comparatively small, possibly indicating small group sizes of two to three individuals.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had acute senses of smell and balance but poor hearing.
facts.quote: The senses of smell and balance were acute, but hearing was poor.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Thescelosaurus might have been a burrowing animal, based on its acute smell and poor hearing.
facts.quote: It might have been burrowing, as acute smell and poor hearing are typical for modern burrowing animals.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus fossils have been found in formations including the Lance, Frenchman, Hell Creek, and Scollard Formations across Wyoming, North Dakota, South Dakota, Montana, Alberta, and Saskatchewan.
facts.quote: The first specimens were discovered in the Lance Formation of Wyoming, but subsequent discoveries have been made in North Dakota, South Dakota, Montana, Alberta, and Saskatchewan, in geological formations including the Frenchman Formation, Hell Creek Formation, and Scollard Formation.

facts.statement: Scientists now doubt the identification of a fossilized heart in a Thescelosaurus specimen that was unearthed in 1999.
facts.quote: The genus attracted media attention in 2000, when a specimen unearthed in 1999 was interpreted as including a fossilized heart, but scientists now doubt the identification of the object.

facts.statement: William Parks described the species T. warreni in 1926 based on a skeleton found in Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: In 1926, William Parks described the new species T. warreni from a well-preserved skeleton from Alberta, Canada, from what was then known as the Edmonton Formation.

facts.statement: Charles M. Sternberg named the species T. edmontonensis in 1940 based on a skeleton discovered in Rumsey, Alberta.
facts.quote: In 1940, Sternberg named an additional species, T. edmontonensis, based on another articulated skeleton (CMN 8537) that he had discovered in the Edmonton Formation of Rumsey, Alberta.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown collected four Thescelosaurus specimens in Montana in 1906 and 1909.
facts.quote: These include four specimens from the Hell Creek Formation collected by Barnum Brown in Montana in 1906 and 1909

facts.statement: A Thescelosaurus specimen was found in 1892 by Wortman and Peterson at an uncertain location.
facts.quote: one specimen found in 1892 by Wortman and Peterson at an uncertain location

facts.statement: Levi Sternberg found two Thescelosaurus specimens in the Frenchman Formation of Saskatchewan in 1921.
facts.quote: two specimens found in 1921 by Levi Sternberg in the Frenchman Formation of Rocky Creek, Saskatchewan

facts.statement: William J. Morris described three partial Thescelosaurus skeletons in 1976, two found in Montana and one in South Dakota.
facts.quote: William J. Morris described three additional partial skeletons in 1976, two found in the Hell Creek Formation of Garfield County, Montana by preparator Harli Garbani, and one from an unknown location in Harding County, South Dakota.

facts.statement: Peter M. Galton revised the classification of Thescelosaurus in 1995.
facts.quote: Galton revised Thescelosaurus for a second time in 1995.

facts.statement: Peter M. Galton assigned a tooth from the University of California Museum of Paleontology to Bugenasaura in 1999.
facts.quote: In a 1999 study on the anatomy of Bugenasaura, Galton assigned a tooth in the collection of the University of California Museum of Paleontology (UCMP 49611) to the latter.

facts.statement: Clint Boyd and colleagues reassessed Thescelosaurus species in 2009 after discovering new specimens with complete skulls.
facts.quote: After the discovery of additional specimens of Thescelosaurus preserving both the skull and skeleton, Clint Boyd and colleagues reassessed the historic and current species of Thescelosaurus in 2009.

facts.statement: The specimen nicknamed "Willo" has a complete skull that is lower and longer than previously thought.
facts.quote: "Willo" also includes a complete skull, showing that it was much lower and longer than previously thought.

facts.statement: Caleb M. Brown and colleagues named the species T. assiniboiensis in 2011 based on a specimen found in 1968 by Albert Swanston.
facts.quote: Another species, T. assiniboiensis, was named by Caleb M. Brown and colleagues in 2011 based on a specimen (RSM P 1225.1) found in 1968 by Albert Swanston, a museum technician at the Royal Saskatchewan Museum.

facts.statement: A Thescelosaurus specimen was reported found at the Tanis fossil site in North Dakota in 2022, potentially linked to the K-Pg extinction event.
facts.quote: In 2022, news media reported that a specimen of Thescelosaurus was found at the Tanis fossil site in North Dakota, which is thought to show direct signs of the Chicxulub asteroid impact in the Gulf of Mexico that resulted in the K-Pg extinction.

facts.statement: A well-preserved skeleton of T. edmontonensis includes most of the vertebral column, pelvis, limbs, and a complete mandible, the first known for the genus.
facts.quote: It preserves most of the vertebral column, pelvis, legs, scapula, coracoid, arm, and, most significantly, multiple bones of the skull roof and a complete mandible, the first known from Thescelosaurus.

facts.statement: The name Bugenasaura combines Latin and Greek roots meaning large cheek lizard.
facts.quote: The name is a combination of the Latin bu, large and gena, cheek, as well as the Ancient Greek saura, lizard.

facts.statement: The "Willo" specimen shows that the skull of Thescelosaurus is much lower and longer than previously thought.
facts.quote: "Willo" also includes a complete skull, showing that it was much lower and longer than previously thought.

facts.statement: New geological studies separated the Edmonton Formation, placing T. edmontonensis in the younger Scollard Formation.
facts.quote: Newer geology has separated the Edmonton Formation into four formations, with Parksosaurus from the older Horseshoe Canyon Formation and Thescelosaurus edmontonensis from the younger Scollard Formation.

facts.statement: A specimen of Thescelosaurus was found just 5 feet below the Fort Union Formation at the youngest known dinosaur locality.
facts.quote: One of Browns specimens, AMNH 5034, was found just 5 ft below the Fort Union Formation, at the youngest locality from which dinosaurs were found.

facts.statement: Teeth from the Judith River Formation of Montana were once thought to be the oldest occurrence of Thescelosaurus.
facts.quote: These teeth had been assigned to Thescelosaurus cf. neglectus by Ashok Sahni in 1972, which would have been the oldest occurrence of Thescelosaurus.

facts.statement: A tooth assigned to Bugenasaura reportedly came from the Late Jurassic Kimmeridge Clay Formation of England, making it roughly 70 million years older than the type specimen.
facts.quote: Significantly, this tooth reportedly came from the Late Jurassic-era Kimmeridge Clay Formation of Weymouth, England, and therefore is roughly 70 million years older than the Bugenasaura type specimen and from another continent.

facts.statement: The specific name infernalis refers to the lower levels of the Hell Creek Formation where the specimen was found.
facts.quote: The specific name, from the Latin infernalis, belonging to the lower regions, is a reference to the lower levels of the Hell Creek Formation from which it is known.

facts.statement: William J. Morris argued that the ankle anatomy and larger size of a specimen were unique, leading him to name the new species T. garbanii.
facts.quote: Morris concluded that its ankle anatomy and larger size was unique, and therefore named the new species Thescelosaurus garbanii, in honor of the discoverer Garbani.

facts.statement: William J. Morris suggested that T. edmontonensis and T. garbanii might eventually be separated from Thescelosaurus as a new genus.
facts.quote: Therefore, he suggested that T. edmontonensis and T. garbanii may eventually be separated from Thescelosaurus as a new genus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the hindlimb of T. garbanii actually belongs to the pachycephalosaurid Stygimoloch.
facts.quote: There was also the possibility that the hindlimb of T. garbanii did instead belong to the pachycephalosaurid Stygimoloch, which is also known from the Hell Creek Formation and for which the hindlimb was unknown.

facts.statement: Peter M. Galton argued that a tooth assigned to Bugenasaura was possibly mislabelled and actually from the Lance Formation of Wyoming.
facts.quote: Galton argued that it had possibly been mislabelled and was actually from the Lance Formation of Wyoming, but the tooth was first collected before the museum was active in the Lance region.

facts.statement: Due to a lack of diagnostic features, Paul M. Barrett and Susannah Maidment classified a tooth as an indeterminate ornithischian in 2011.
facts.quote: The lack of diagnostic features led Paul M. Barrett and Susannah Maidment to classify the tooth as an indeterminate ornithischian in 2011.

facts.statement: Clint Boyd and colleagues considered the new combination T. infernalis to be undiagnostic.
facts.quote: By reassigning the species, Boyd and colleagues created the new combination T. infernalis which they considered undiagnostic.

facts.statement: The assignment of most Thescelosaurus specimens to specific species remained uncertain due to a lack of overlapping bone material for comparison.
facts.quote: Specimens can only be directly compared if they preserve the same bones, but overlapping material is often not available – the assignment of most Thescelosaurus specimens to any of the three recognized species therefore remained uncertain.

facts.statement: The largest known thescelosaurid had an estimated body length of 2.5 to 4.0 meters and a weight of 200 to 300 kilograms.
facts.quote: The largest known thescelosaurid, its body length has been estimated at 2.5 – 4.0 m and the weight at 200 – 300 kg

facts.statement: The large type specimen of T. garbanii was estimated to be 4 to 4.5 meters long.
facts.quote: with the large type specimen of T. garbanii estimated at 4 – 4.5 m long

facts.statement: It is possible that Thescelosaurus was sexually dimorphic, with one sex being larger than the other.
facts.quote: It may have been sexually dimorphic, with one sex larger than the other

facts.statement: The skull of Thescelosaurus had a long, low snout ending in a toothless beak.
facts.quote: The skull had a long, low snout that ended in a toothless beak

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had long rod-like bones called palpebrals above its eyes, creating heavy bony eyebrows.
facts.quote: Long rod-like bones called palpebrals were present above the eyes, giving the animal heavy bony eyebrows

facts.statement: The premaxillae of Thescelosaurus had six teeth each, a primitive trait also found in earlier forms like Lesothosaurus and Scutellosaurus.
facts.quote: The premaxillae had six teeth each, a primitive trait among ornithischians that is otherwise only found in much earlier and more basal forms such as Lesothosaurus and Scutellosaurus

facts.statement: T. neglectus had six sacral vertebrae and twenty-seven presacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: T. neglectus had 6 sacral ("hip") vertebrae and 27 presacral ("neck and back") vertebrae

facts.statement: The tail of Thescelosaurus was long, comprising half of the total body length.
facts.quote: The tail was long and made up half of the total body length

facts.statement: Large, thin, flat mineralized plates known as intercostal plates were found next to the ribs of Thescelosaurus.
facts.quote: Large thin and flat mineralized plates have been found next to the ribs' sides, so-called intercostal plates

facts.statement: The femur was longer than the tibia in Thescelosaurus, distinguishing it from closely related genera.
facts.quote: The femur (thigh bone) was longer than the tibia (shin bone), which distinguishes the genus from closely related genera

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had short, broad, five-fingered hands.
facts.quote: Thescelosaurus had short, broad, five-fingered hands

facts.statement: Only the first three digits of Thescelosaurus ended in hooflike unguals.
facts.quote: Only the first three digits ended in hooflike unguals

facts.statement: The foot of Thescelosaurus had five metatarsals, but only the first four carried digits, while the fifth was vestigial.
facts.quote: The foot had five metatarsals, though only the first four carried digits, with the fifth metatarsal being vestigial (reduced to a small splint)

facts.statement: Most of Thescelosaurus's weight was supported by the center three digits, with the middle (third) digit being the longest.
facts.quote: Most of the animal's weight was therefore supported by the center three digits, of which the middle (third) was the longest

facts.statement: T. garbanii differs from other species in having a unique ankle where the calcaneus is reduced and does not contribute to the midtarsal joint.
facts.quote: The species T. garbanii differs from the other species in its unique ankle, with the calcaneus being reduced and not contributing to the midtarsal joint

facts.statement: In 2022, it was reported that skin impressions on the Tanis specimen show that parts of Thescelosaurus were covered in scales.
facts.quote: In 2022, news media reported that the Tanis specimen preserves skin impressions on a leg that show that parts of the animal were covered in scales

facts.statement: Morris suggested that Thescelosaurus had armor in the form of small scutes along the midline of the neck, though this is debated.
facts.quote: Morris suggested that armor was present, in the form of small scutes he interpreted as located at least along the midline of the neck of one specimen

facts.statement: Galton argued in 2008 that the scutes interpreted by Morris were of crocodilian origin.
facts.quote: Galton argued in 2008 that Morris's scutes are crocodilian in origin

facts.statement: Gilmore described Thescelosaurus in 1913 and initially classified it within the family Camptosauridae.
facts.quote: In his 1913 description of Thescelosaurus, Gilmore considered it to be a member of Camptosauridae, alongside Hypsilophodon, Dryosaurus and Laosaurus.

facts.statement: In 1915, Gilmore reclassified Thescelosaurus into the family Hypsilophodontidae.
facts.quote: In 1915, he instead placed it within Hypsilophodontidae alongside only Hypsilophodon.

facts.statement: Galton classified Thescelosaurus as an iguanodontid in 1974 based on leg proportions but reverted to hypsilophodontid in 1995 after finding Iguanodontidae to be polyphyletic.
facts.quote: Galton classified Thescelosaurus as a member of Iguanodontidae based on hindlimb proportions in 1974, but this family was found to be polyphyletic (not a natural group); he therefore returned to a hypsilophodontid classification in 1995.

facts.statement: Boyd and colleagues identified a clade of early ornithopods including Thescelosaurus, Parksosaurus, Zephyrosaurus, Orodromeus, and Oryctodromeus.
facts.quote: Boyd and colleagues found support for a larger group of early ornithopods consisting of Thescelosaurus, Parksosaurus, Zephyrosaurus, Orodromeus and Oryctodromeus.

facts.statement: In 2013, Boyd and colleagues reintroduced the family name Thescelosauridae, dividing it into the subfamilies Thescelosaurinae and Orodrominae.
facts.quote: The same authors confirmed these results again in 2013, prompting them to reintroduce the name Thescelosauridae for the entire group, which was divided into the revised subfamily Thescelosaurinae and the new subfamily Orodrominae.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Thescelosaurus and its relatives belong to Ornithopoda or represent a more basal group.
facts.quote: There is also disagreement about whether Thescelosaurus and thescelosaurids are members of Ornithopoda or more basal.

facts.statement: Boyd argued in 2015 that there was no definitive evidence Thescelosaurus was an ornithopod because many studies lacked marginocephalians or were unresolved.
facts.quote: Boyd highlighted in 2015 that many phylogenetic studies that included Thescelosaurus either do not include marginocephalians or are unresolved, so there was no definitive evidence that Thescelosaurus was an ornithopod.

facts.statement: The genus Thescelosaurus was named by Gilmore in 1913.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Gilmore, 1913

facts.statement: The type species of Thescelosaurus is Thescelosaurus neglectus.
facts.quote: type_species: Thescelosaurus neglectus

facts.statement: Bugenasaura is a synonym of Thescelosaurus, proposed by Galton in 1995.
facts.quote: synonyms: Bugenasaura Galton, 1995

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous, approximately between 72 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivieron a finales del período Cretácico, aproximadamente entre 72 y 66 millones de años, desde el Campaniense al Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus was a bipedal ornithopod measuring approximately 2.5 to 4 meters in length.
facts.quote: Este ornitópodo bípedo se conoce por varios esqueletos parciales y los cráneos que indican que medían alrededor de 2,5 a 4 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had robust hind limbs, small and broad hands, and a head with a very elongated snout.
facts.quote: Tenía los miembros traseros robustos, las manos pequeñas y anchas, y una cabeza con un hocico muy alargado.

facts.statement: The preservation and completeness of many specimens suggest Thescelosaurus may have preferred living near water currents.
facts.quote: La preservación y lo completo de muchos de sus especímenes indican que pudo haber preferido vivir cerca de corrientes de agua.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus likely fed selectively based on its different tooth types and narrow snout.
facts.quote: The different types of teeth, as well as the narrow snout, suggest that it was a selective feeder.

facts.statement: One specimen of Thescelosaurus exhibited a bone pathology where the long bones of the right foot were fused at the top.
facts.quote: One specimen is known to have had a bone pathology, with the long bones of the right foot fused at their tops.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus was estimated to be 2.5 to 4 meters long and weigh between 200 and 300 kilograms based on various specimens.
facts.quote: El tamaño del animal se ha estimado entre los 2,5 a 4.metros de largo, a partir de varios especímenes, y un peso de entre 200 a 300 kilogramos

facts.statement: The large type specimen of T. garbanii is estimated to be 4 to 4.5 meters long.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo grande de T. garbanii se estima en 4 a 4,5 metros de largo

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus was a bipedal animal with a strong constitution.
facts.quote: Thescelosaurus era un animal bípedo de constitución fuerte

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus possessed robust hind legs, small and wide hands, an elongated and pointed snout, and likely small armored plates along its spine.
facts.quote: Poseía patas traseras robustas, pequeñas y amplias "manos", un morro alargado y puntiagudo, y probablemente pequeñas placas armados a lo largo de la columna

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had a prominent bone border along its entire upper jaw and lower jaw to support muscular cheeks.
facts.quote: Tenía un prominente borde a lo largo de todo su maxilar El soporte óseo para las mejillas, y un borde en ambos dentarios

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had two types of teeth: small pointed teeth at the front and leaf-shaped teeth in the cheeks.
facts.quote: Los dientes eran de dos dos tipos, pequeños dientes puntiagudos al frente y dientes con forma de hojas en las mejillas

facts.statement: Thin bone plates were found alongside Thescelosaurus' ribs and sides, but their function remains unknown.
facts.quote: Se han encontrado finas placas de hueso junto a sus costados y costillas, siendo su función desconocida hasta el momento

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had short, wide hands with five fingers and walked on the tips of its four-toed feet, which ended in a hoof-like structure formed by the last phalanx.
facts.quote: Tenía las manos cortas, amplias, con cinco dedos, pisaba con la punta de los cuatro dedos de cada pie terminados en una especie de casco formada por la última falange de cada dedo

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had teeth in the premaxilla (upper beak), a primitive trait among ornithopods, and long bar-like bones called brow horns over its eyes, giving it heavy bony eyebrows.
facts.quote: El cráneo también tenía dientes en el premaxilar, o pico superior, un rasgo primitivo entre ornitópodos, y huesos similares a barras largos llamados palpebrales sobre los ojos, dándole unas pesadas cejas huesudas

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus was likely a herbivore but could also have been an omnivore.
facts.quote: Thescelosaurus fue un robusto bípedo, probablemente herbívoro, pero también podría ser omnívoro

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus likely fed on vegetation within the first five meters of the ground, storing food in its cheeks to chew later.
facts.quote: Debió alimentarse en los primeros cinco metros desde el suelo, seleccionado el alimento, y almacenándolos en sus mejillas para poder luego masticarlos

facts.statement: One specimen showed a bone pathology in the right metatarsus where it fused with others, hindering rapid movement.
facts.quote: Un espécimen presenta una patología ósea, en el metatarso del pie derecho y se fundió en los otros, obstaculizando el movimiento rápido

facts.statement: It is debated whether Thescelosaurus could have moved on all fours due to its long arms and wide hands, though this idea is not widely accepted in scientific literature.
facts.quote: Este animal pudo haberse movido sobre sus cuatro miembros, dados que sus brazos eran lo bastante largos y sus manos anchas, pero esta idea no se ha tenido en cuenta en la literatura científica

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus belongs to the parent group Thescelosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Thescelosaurinae

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus is classified in the family Thescelosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Thescelosauridae

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus lived from the Turonian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 93.9 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Maastrichtian (93.9 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus may have exhibited sexual dimorphism, with one sex being larger than the other.
facts.quote: Pudo haber tenido dimorfismo sexual, con un sexo de mayor tamaño que el otro
